cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Domestic – relating to the home, household, or family life.

p.em: Example: She managed domestic chores while reflecting on her life.

cosy-blockquote.p: Resilience – the capacity to recover quickly from difficulties.

p.em: Example: Her resilience helped her bounce back after every setback.

cosy-blockquote.p: Routine – a sequence of actions regularly followed.

p.em: Example: Washing dishes and paying bills are part of daily routine.

cosy-blockquote.p: Breakdown – a mechanical failure or emotional collapse.

p.em: Example: A sudden emotional breakdown forced her to stop and rest.

cosy-blockquote.p: Optimism – hopefulness and confidence about the future.

p.em: Example: She maintained her optimism even when things went wrong.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cycle – a series of events that are regularly repeated.

p.em: Example: Life moves in a continuous cycle of ups and downs.

cosy-blockquote.p: Predictable – able to be foreseen or expected.

p.em: Example: When life becomes too predictable, we crave new adventures.

cosy-blockquote.p: Struggle – make forceful efforts to get free of restraint or task.

p.em: Example: He continued to struggle through difficult emotional moments.

cosy-blockquote.p: Connection – a relationship in which a person or thing is linked.

p.em: Example: Deep human connection helps us survive life's storms.

cosy-blockquote.p: Comfort – a state of physical ease and freedom from pain.

p.em: Example: Finding comfort in simple habits keeps us grounded.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: Love is coming around back → Correct: Love is coming around again ((Use 'coming around again' to express cyclic reoccurrence.))
Incorrect: I believe to → Correct: I believe in ((Use preposition 'in' after 'believe' when expressing trust or faith.))
Incorrect: Nothing stays the same like → Correct: Nothing stays the same as ((Use 'the same as' for identity or equality.))
